newsitem.title: EGYPT: Mubarak-Netanyahu meet constructive sign - Britain.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak-Netanyahu meet constructive sign - Britain.

text.p: Britain's Foreign Office minister met senior Egyptian officials on Monday and described a planned summit between Egyptian and Israeli leaders as a constructive development in the region.

Derek Fatchett, the first British minister to visit Egypt since the Labour Party won the general elections this month, told reporters after meeting Foreign Minister Amr Moussa and President Hosni Mubarak's adviser Osama el-Baz:
"We had a long and very constructive talk about the future of the peace process in the Middle East."
"I am delighted that President Mubarak and (Israeli) Prime Minister (Benjamin) Netanyahu are meeting. That is in itself a constructive sign," he said. "Let us hope that it is successful."
The Egyptian and Israeli leaders are to meet on Tuesday in the Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh to explore ways to revive Middle East peace talks.

Fatchett said his country was willing to take part in the peacemaking deadlocked since March when Israel started building the Jewish settlement on the hillside called Har Homa, or Jabal Abu Ghneim, in Arab East Jerusalem.
"We are keen to play a constructive role...within the European Union," he said.
